cases.expected: Rule.isSatisfied(index) returns true for any index where the underlying NumericIndicator value is less than 10, and false otherwise.
cases.description: Standard case: a positive integer constant. The method should create a ConstantIndicator with value 10 and return an UnderIndicatorRule that correctly evaluates the '<' relationship.

cases.expected: Rule.isSatisfied(index) returns true when the underlying NumericIndicator value is negative, false when it is zero or positive.
cases.description: Boundary case with zero. Verifies that the rule treats zero as the threshold and respects the strict less‑than semantics.

cases.expected: Rule.isSatisfied(index) returns true only when the underlying NumericIndicator value is less than -5 (i.e., more negative), false otherwise.
cases.description: Negative constant: ensures that the method works correctly with negative numbers and does not mistakenly invert the comparison.

cases.expected: Rule.isSatisfied(index) returns true for values < 3.14159, false for values ≥ 3.14159.
cases.description: Floating‑point constant (Double). Checks that the method correctly handles non‑integral Number implementations.

cases.expected: NullPointerException (or IllegalArgumentException) thrown by createConstant when the argument is null.
cases.description: Null argument: verifies that the method validates its input and fails fast when a null Number is supplied.

cases.expected: Rule.isSatisfied(index) returns true for values < 100, false otherwise.
cases.description: BigDecimal constant: tests that the method works with arbitrary‑precision Number subclasses.

cases.expected: Rule.isSatisfied(index) returns true for every index where the underlying NumericIndicator value is a finite number (i.e., all typical values), because no realistic value can be greater than or equal to Long.MAX_VALUE.
cases.description: Very large positive constant (Long.MAX_VALUE) – verifies that the rule works correctly when the threshold is far beyond any possible indicator value.

cases.expected: Rule.isSatisfied(index) returns true for indices whose value is negative or exactly zero, and false for any positive value ≥ Double.MIN_VALUE.
cases.description: Smallest positive non‑zero double – tests the strict‑less‑than semantics around the zero boundary.

cases.expected: Rule.isSatisfied(index) returns true when the underlying value < 5.5f, false otherwise.
cases.description: Float constant – ensures that the method correctly handles Float Number implementations.

cases.expected: Rule.isSatisfied(index) returns true for values < 2 (as a short), false otherwise.
cases.description: Short constant – verifies handling of smaller integral Number types.

cases.expected: Rule.isSatisfied(index) returns true for values < -1, false for -1 and greater.
cases.description: Byte constant – tests the method with the smallest integral wrapper type.

cases.expected: Rule.isSatisfied(index) always returns false (the rule never satisfies) because any comparison with NaN is defined as false.
cases.description: NaN constant – checks that the rule fails fast for an undefined numeric threshold.

cases.expected: Rule.isSatisfied(index) returns true for every finite underlying value (including negative, zero, and positive numbers), and false only when the underlying value is NaN.
cases.description: Positive infinity – validates that the rule treats infinity as an upper bound that all finite numbers are less than.

cases.expected: Rule.isSatisfied(index) always returns false because no numeric value (including -Infinity itself) is less than negative infinity.
cases.description: Negative infinity – ensures the rule never satisfies when the threshold is the lowest possible double.

cases.expected: Rule.isSatisfied(index) returns true for underlying values < 12345678901234567890, false otherwise.
cases.description: BigInteger constant – tests compatibility with another arbitrary‑precision Number subclass.

cases.expected: Rule.isSatisfied(index) returns true when the underlying value is negative, false when it is zero or positive.
cases.description: Zero as a Double – confirms that the method behaves identically for zero expressed as a floating‑point Number.

cases.expected: NullPointerException thrown because the NumericIndicator instance was created with a null delegate (e.g., NumericIndicator.of(null)). The method attempts to create a ConstantIndicator and then build an UnderIndicatorRule, which dereferences the null delegate.
cases.description: NumericIndicator without an underlying delegate. Verifies that isLessThan fails fast when the instance is improperly initialized.

cases.expected: RuntimeException (or subclass) propagated from the FaultyNumber.doubleValue() call during constant creation.
cases.description: Custom Number implementation whose doubleValue() throws an exception. Ensures that isLessThan does not swallow unexpected runtime errors from the Number argument.
